title: A 2-second AI opener, then real Cat Sort gameplay: our short-form promo workflow
author: ElaGameStudio
selftext:
We are the developers of Cat Sort Bubble Puzzle, a Unity sorting game for Android. AI-assisted kitten artwork is part of the visual workflow. For this new short, we used an existing game-art image as the character/style reference and generated a separate promotional illustration. Here is what we actually put together.



The prompt asked for a lavender kitten in an iridescent bubble, the same plush character style, a dark uncluttered area for text, and explicitly no HUD or fake game buttons. We added the question “Which cat would you pick?” in the edit rather than asking the image model to render the lettering. A small zoom animates this still for the first two seconds.



At second two, the video cuts to 18 seconds of actual gameplay. The five waiting spots filling up are the central decision, and the clip shows the failed attempt. The final three seconds show the real game title and Android call to action. We kept the generated illustration separate from the gameplay and disclosed the AI opener in the captions. The art supplies the character close-up; the real recording has to explain the mechanic.



The soundtrack is an original 128 BPM composition synthesized in Python with plucked notes, bass and percussion, then mixed into the 23-second edit in FFmpeg. No third-party song or sampled recording was used. This is a fresh creative; we do not have a measured retention or install-lift result for it yet.



Would you open with the kitten close-up, or lead with the crowded waiting spots and use the AI art as the end card instead?



The finished short: [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/NwgR6Zbpagg](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/NwgR6Zbpagg)

Android download: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.Meetagame.CatSortBubblePuzzle](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.Meetagame.CatSortBubblePuzzle)

The game is free to download, with ads and optional in-app purchases.
